elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: The rendered Section 10 carve-out reads "Except for assignment to a successor upon written notice to the other party" — there is no affiliate exception, so a Company assignment to an affiliate still needs Contractor's prior written consent. To meet this element the carve-out would have to read, e.g., "Except for assignment by Company to an affiliate or to a successor...".

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: "Except for assignment to a successor upon written notice to the other party, neither party shall assign...without the other party's express, prior written consent" — the unqualified term "successor" covers a successor by merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, and the exception removes the consent requirement for Company.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The new carve-out is mutual ("neither party shall assign...Except for assignment to a successor"), so Contractor may now assign to its own successor without Company's consent. Preferred level requires the successor freedom to run one way only (Customer side).

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Retained language: consent "will not be unreasonably withheld", applied mutually and therefore to Company's consent to a Contractor assignment.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: No competitor prohibition appears anywhere in Section 10 as rendered; an express "and in no event to a competitor of Company" limitation would be required.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Condition does not arise: the document contains no change-of-control trigger and no deemed-assignment language; Section 6 termination rights are convenience/breach based and not tied to a change of control, so no Vendor exit right exists to delete.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: "Except for assignment to a successor upon written notice to the other party, neither party shall assign..." — the exception is symmetrical and permits either party to assign to a successor.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: The carve-out is expressly conditioned: "assignment to a successor upon written notice to the other party".

Retained: "neither party shall assign, transfer, or subcontract this Agreement or any of its obligations hereunder without the other party's express, prior written consent". The only no-consent exception added is the successor exception itself; no affiliate or other non-successor exception is retained or introduced.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Retained: "which will not be unreasonably withheld", attaching to the consent requirement for all non-successor assignments, transfers and subcontracts.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete on the operative text: the inserted lead-in creates a mutual successor-assignment right on written notice, and the pre-existing consent plus not-unreasonably-withheld mechanics survive verbatim to cover the remaining two elements.

Preferred level is not reached: no affiliate carve-out for Company, no competitor bar on Contractor assignment, and the successor carve-out is mutual so Contractor can also assign without Company's consent. If the drafter wants preferred, the edit must be one-directional ("Except for an assignment by Company to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets, upon written notice...") and add "and in no event to a competitor of Company".

The change-of-control element is satisfied vacuously — the agreement contains no change-of-control or deemed-assignment trigger and no Vendor termination right keyed to one, so nothing needs deleting.

Minimality holds: a single inserted exception clause; the existing mutual prohibition, the subcontracting reference, the express prior written consent requirement and the reasonableness standard are all retained unchanged, with no survival tails, notice procedures, or other extras.

Intent is preserved: no defined term is disturbed, no cross-reference is left dangling, and the retained sentence is internally consistent with the new exception (the exception is drafted as a carve-out from, not a contradiction of, the consent requirement). Note only that "successor" is left undefined; if counterparty resists, tightening it to "successor in interest by merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets" would remove ambiguity without changing the position.

The "deviation" classification is supportable: as originally drafted every assignment, including a corporate-transaction successor assignment, was gated on the other party's consent, which fails the fallback's mutual successor-on-notice element.
